The most common cause is that the **parent** component re-renders, which triggers all children to re-render by default, even if their props haven't changed. A few things to check: **Parent is re-rendering** — Every time the parent renders (state update, context change, or its own parent updating), children re-render too. The props might be identical, but React still runs the child function. **Props are new objects/arrays/functions each render** — If the parent creates props inline like ` {}} data={[]}/>`, those are new references on every render. React sees different objects and re-renders the child. Same content, different object identity. **No memoization** — Add `React.memo` around the child to skip re-renders when props don't change by reference: ```javascript const Child = React.memo(({ name, value }) => { return
{name}: {value}
}); ``` **Child has its own state** — If the child has `useState` or other state that changes, it re-renders regardless of props. **Context changes** — If the child uses `useContext` and that context updates, it re-renders even if you don't pass context as a prop. To debug, add a `console.log` in the child component body — you'll see every time it actually runs. Then use React DevTools Profiler to see what triggered the parent to re-render in the first place. What's the setup — are you using `React.memo`, and where are the props coming from?
